text:
amelia: FYI we got a customer report — calls to tool 'fetch_customer_profile' started returning 400 schema validation with message 'tool not found' after a rename yesterday. Happening only for one tenant (acme-corp) on private deployment.
hao: Can you paste the failing request + error payload and which region/private release? Also did they call by alias or UUID?
amelia: Calling by alias. Here is the request they sent (redacted):
```
POST /v1/call_tool
{
  "tool": "fetch_customer_profilé",  # note the e with acute (maybe unicode)
  "args": { "customer_id": "C-123" }
}
```
Response: 400 {"error":"tool not found","code":"tool_lookup_failed","lookup_key":"fetch_customer_profil5"}
(support-bot: they included the exact bytes in logs, looks like the alias is in NFD form on the client)
support-bot: registry-sync: last full sync for tenant acme-corp @ 1717620000; incremental queue processed up to 1717640000; alias-cache TTL 300s; recent rename event 1717609000
hao: Hmm. Did the rename change the alias spelling/diacritics? We had one rename where display name used a composed char and registry stored decomposed.
sophie: I pulled the registry entry for the tool on the private control plane: alias stored as "fetch_customer_profil5" (decomposed e + accent). The model onboarding pipeline normalized to NFC and the UI shows "fetch_customer_profilé" (composed). Client calls are using the composed char. Lookup logic currently does a straight string compare without unicode normalization -> mismatch.
jordan: So two different normalizations live in the system. That explains intermittent failures after the rename rolled out. Private registry was backfilled with NFD strings during an earlier migration and the hosted onboarding is NFC.
amelia: Customer impact: ~15% of their calls hit the mismatch (clients vary); they see 400 + schema validation because tool found = null -> default endpoint rejects payload shape.
hao: Repro steps requested for oncall/eng: can we reproduce locally? Steps I recommend: 1) curl to registry to show stored alias bytes, 2) simulate call with composed vs decomposed alias to the private gateway, 3) check gateway logs for the exact lookup key.
sophie: Repro commands: 
1) Check registry alias raw bytes:
```
curl -s -H 'X-Tenant: acme-corp' https://private-registry.internal/tools?alias=fetch_customer_profil%C3%A9 | jq .items[0].alias_bytes
# returns e.g. [102,101,116,99,104,..., 101, 772]  # 772 = combining acute
```
2) Failing call (composed):
```
curl -s -X POST https://private-gateway.acme.example/v1/call_tool -d '{"tool":"fetch_customer_profil%C3%A9","args":{}}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -D -
```
3) Successful call (use UUID):
```
curl -X POST https://private-gateway.acme.example/v1/call_tool -d '{"tool":"tool_01F...UUID","args":{}}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```
support-bot: mitigation checklist created: incident-#1234, assigned to eng-ml.
hao: Short-term mitigation for the customer: ask them to call by tool UUID (works immediately) OR we can add an alias entry mapped from the composed form to the existing tool in the registry (hotfix). Which do we prefer? Amelia can push a temporary alias mapping.
amelia: I'll ask the customer to switch to UUID while we patch. Also can add alias mapping if they want immediate fix.
sophie: Long-term fix: normalize incoming alias lookups to NFC before comparing; also run a backfill to canonicalize existing aliases to NFC in the private registry and purge ambiguous duplicates. Patch queued with code review (PR #4621) to apply normalization in the gateway and registry lookup layer.
jordan: Also add a unit test and a fuzz test for unicode decomposition coverage — caught this in a very old migration but we didn't have coverage.
hao: Priority: P2 customer impact. Action items: Amelia to confirm customer switch to UUID or request alias hotfix; Sophie to land normalization PR and schedule backfill; Jordan to add tests; I'll monitor metrics for 24h.
amelia: Confirmed customer will use UUID for now. They requested hotfix too; I'll file the alias create request (tenant-scoped) and cc eng.
support-bot: alias-create-request submitted (req-789); scheduled window 1717659000-1717662600. :white_check_mark:
sophie: Note for postmortem: also check registry sync path to ensure no new migrations write NFD bytes. Add normalization into ingestion pipeline.
hao: Thanks all. Logging note: if you see tool_lookup_failed with lookup_key bytes ending in 772 (combining acute) that's our fingerprint.
amelia: Closing loop with customer and updating ticket with mitigation steps. :thumbsup:
